scope: Independent adversarial release security review of the CORRECTED ArrTags v1.2.0.0 release candidate. Three things: (1) re-verify that SEC-21.5-01 (the provider clients followed HTTP redirects and re-sent X-Api-Key to the 3xx Location origin) is actually resolved by the task 21.7 fix, by inspecting the code AND by independently reproducing both the pre-fix egress and the post-fix non-egress against the SHIPPED assembly rather than trusting the task reports; (2) re-verify the carried SEC-21.5-02, SEC-21.5-03, SEC-21.5-04 LOW findings and the INFORMATIONAL confirmations, re-running their reproductions against the shipped assembly; (3) re-audit the corrected whole candidate across the v1.2 surfaces (ADR-025 diagnostics, ADR-026 log subject, ADR-028 settings, ADR-022/ADR-029 cursor, ADR-023 re-enqueue, ADR-024 restore, ADR-027 size) and release breadth (ADR-005 secrets/leases and provider transport, ADR-012 webhook, state integrity, bounded inputs, packaged artifact), plus byte-consistency of the packaged ArrTags.dll with a clean build of the audited source. No product code, test, canonical document, PLANS.md, docs/plan/state.json, manifest.json, or release artifact was modified; no commit or tag was created. Reviewer-owned temporary material lives under /tmp/final-review/security/21.10/.

sec_21_5_01_disposition: RESOLVED. Independently verified, not accepted on the strength of the task 21.7 report. The fix is present in the source and in the SHIPPED binary, and my own reviewer-authored reproduction against the shipped assembly (extracted from artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip) both (a) shows no egress with the shipped registration and (b) leaks the key with the pre-fix registration while running the identical shipped client/lease code path, which proves the harness discriminates and that the fix is what closes the gap. Finding SEC-21.5-01 is therefore carried with severity MEDIUM and status 'resolved'. The fix also introduced no new reachable path for the credential and no weakening of any other transport property (see SEC-21.10-01 for the one factually inaccurate rationale recorded in the task 21.7 worker report, which is INFORMATIONAL and does not reopen the gate).

findings.area: secret / provider transport boundary (credential forwarded across an HTTP redirect)
findings.summary: The finding recorded by the task 21.5 review is closed. At HEAD 2072ec1 all four named provider clients are registered with a primary handler whose AllowAutoRedirect is false (strict Sonarr, strict Radarr, and both opt-in .Insecure clients), so the X-Api-Key header applied by SecretLease.ApplyTo can no longer be re-sent across a 3xx hop; and both ClassifyStatus methods now have an explicit >=300 and <400 arm that fails closed as the bounded InvalidResponse / ArrErrorRetryability.Never provider error with a fixed code-owned message. I verified this three ways: source inspection, reflection over the two private handler factories and over the resolved HttpClientFactoryOptions of all four names in the SHIPPED assembly, and a reviewer-authored two-origin loopback reproduction run against the SHIPPED assembly. The reproduction also includes a pre-fix control (a bare AddHttpClient(name) factory substituted for the plugin's own) that runs the identical shipped SonarrClient + SecretLease code and DOES deliver the API key to the second origin, so the negative result is attributable to the fix rather than to a harness that cannot observe the leak. The 3xx path additionally never reads the provider's response body (ClassifyStatus returns a non-null, non-Later error and SendAsync returns immediately), so a provider-controlled 3xx body, header, or Location value has no route into memory, a log line, or a persisted state.

findings.area: log path disclosure / bounded log subject (ADR-026)
findings.summary: Carried LOW, re-verified at HEAD 2072ec1 and reproduced against the SHIPPED assembly; unchanged and not a v1.2 or 21.7 regression. LogSubject.Create uses Path.GetFileName with host-platform separator semantics, so on the pinned Linux host a backslash is a legal file-name character and a Windows-style or UNC primary path is emitted whole, disclosing a user account name and a full directory chain contrary to the ADR-026 clause 1 directory/full-path exclusion. The exposure is bounded (128 scalars, and a real Jellyfin media path on the pinned host cannot carry a backslash) and involves no secret, so it stays LOW. The related SR-15.4-04 observation (Path.GetFileName is a path splitter, not a URL parser) is re-confirmed unreachable-for-practice and remains folded in.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:47-68 ('var fileName = Path.GetFileName(primaryPath);' with no host-platform normalization)

reproduction against the SHIPPED assembly: 'C:\\Users\\admin\\Videos\\secret.mkv' -> 32 of 32 scalars emitted whole; '\\\\fileserver\\media\\secret\\file.mkv' -> 34 of 34 scalars emitted whole; positive controls confirm the POSIX contract holds ('/media/movies/Example.mkv' -> 'Example.mkv'; '/srv/media/4K Movies/Some.Movie.2019.mkv' -> 'Some.Movie.2019.mkv'); a 300-scalar name truncates to exactly 128; a whitespace-only path falls back to the item identifier

findings.area: provider transport / decision rationale accuracy (ADR-005, new in the 21.7 fix)
findings.summary: New observation, no defect. The 21.7 fix installs an explicit HttpClientHandler as the primary handler for all four named clients. On the pinned .NET 10 runtime the IHttpClientFactory default primary handler is actually System.Net.Http.SocketsHttpHandler, not HttpClientHandler, so the task 21.7 worker report's stated rationale ('The .NET client factory's default primary handler is HttpClientHandler, so using the same type preserves every other default') is factually wrong for this runtime. The conclusion it reaches is nevertheless correct and I verified it: unwrapping the installed HttpClientHandler to its internal SocketsHttpHandler shows an effective transport configuration identical to the factory default in every security-relevant property (SslOptions.AllowRenegotiation/AllowRsaPkcs1Padding/AllowRsaPssPadding/AllowTlsResume all true, CertificateRevocationCheckMode NoCheck, EncryptionPolicy RequireEncryption, EnabledSslProtocols None, RemoteCertificateValidationCallback null for the strict handler, UseCookies true, UseProxy true, Credentials null, DefaultProxyCredentials null, PreAuthenticate false, AutomaticDecompression None, MaxAutomaticRedirections 50, ConnectTimeout and PooledConnectionLifetime identical, EnableMultipleHttp2Connections false, ActivityHeadersPropagator W3C). The only difference is AllowAutoRedirect=False, which is the fix. Recorded so the recorded rationale is accurate and so any future 'we only changed redirect following' claim is stated against the real baseline. The narrower SurfaceDnsEmptyLabel/content-buffering differences of the legacy HttpClientHandler surface are not reachable for this integration, which is GET-only with no request body.
evidence: reproduction at /tmp/final-review/security/21.10/default-handler: 'FACTORY DEFAULT: unwrapped=System.Net.Http.SocketsHttpHandler ... AllowAutoRedirect = True' versus 'FIX INSTALLED : unwrapped=System.Net.Http.SocketsHttpHandler ... AllowAutoRedirect = False', with the SslOptions and connection-property dumps identical line for line apart from the redirect flag
docs/implementation/21.7/worker-report.json interpretations[1] ('HttpClientHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=false', basis: 'The .NET client factory's default primary handler is HttpClientHandler')
src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:241-262 (the two handler factories)

src/ArrTags/Providers/Sonarr/SonarrClient.cs:287 and src/ArrTags/Providers/Radarr/RadarrClient.cs:261 remain the only HttpRequestMessage construction sites, both HttpMethod.Get, so no request body is ever buffered by the legacy handler surface
findings.recommended_action: No code change. Correct the recorded rationale in docs/implementation/21.7/worker-report.json or the next task report so it says the factory default on this runtime is SocketsHttpHandler and that the effective settings were verified equivalent (history is otherwise immutable). If the constraint is ever relaxed, note that the strict/insecure split is expressed through HttpClientHandler.ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback and would need a SocketsHttpHandler.SslOptions form instead.

findings.area: state integrity / versioned envelope, quarantine vs discard, lifecycle fence, write-ahead publication
findings.summary: Re-verified unchanged at HEAD 2072ec1 (no state, artwork, or reconciliation file changed since the 21.5 review). State is written through AtomicFileWriter (a FileMode.CreateNew temp file in the same directory, Flush(flushToDisk:true), then File.Move overwrite, with the temp file removed on failure), so a torn write cannot replace a good record. A cache record that fails the envelope check is deleted and reported as Discarded; an authoritative record is moved to quarantine with its bytes preserved plus a 512-character-bounded reason file and is never treated as absent, and a failed quarantine leaves the original in place. Records are capped at 4 MiB on write and enumeration is bounded and materialized before any record is read. PluginStatePaths validates both segments as single path components. The v1.2 cursor and the fence and publisher write-ahead ordering are unchanged.
evidence: src/ArrTags/State/AtomicFileWriter.cs:30-60 and src/ArrTags/State/StateRepository.cs:88-104, 205-216 (Cache -> TryDeleteRecord + Discarded; Authoritative -> StateQuarantine.TryQuarantine + Quarantined)

findings.area: plugin configuration / ADR-028 byte-unit settings surface
findings.summary: Re-verified unchanged at HEAD 2072ec1. The byte-denominated limits are converted page-side with a code-owned unit/step/precision table, byteLimitToBytes returns null for any value that is not an exact step multiple, and readByteLimitValues aborts the submit before any POST, so a partial set is never sent. The server independently enforces the validated byte range on save and on load; the step alignment is deliberately page-side only, exactly as ADR-028 clause 1 specifies and as the 21.4/21.9 live matrices recorded (F-21.4-4 / V12-G6-1). A saved value therefore cannot widen a limit or inject into a URL, filesystem path, fingerprint, or log line. The reviewed page is the served page.

findings.area: bounded input / persisted reconciliation cursor (ADR-022, ADR-029)
findings.summary: Re-verified unchanged at HEAD 2072ec1. The cursor is a single fixed-kind ('reconciliation-cursor'), fixed-id ('current'), versioned, integrity-checked Cache-authority record; it carries only the bounded scope identity and the opaque (SortName, itemId) position, never a path, provider payload, or credential; a failed envelope check, a failed semantic Validate, or a scope mismatch is a miss that resets to the start rather than a quarantine or a trust; and the fixed code-owned kind and id mean no attacker-influenced value reaches a filesystem path. Write is bounded (4,096 ids, 256-character ids, 512-character SortName hint) and any write failure is contained by LibraryReconciliationService.AdvanceCursor so the run completes. The two honest observations recorded at 21.5 stand unchanged: the scope identity is built from the unbounded EnabledLibraries list (carried SEC-11), so a pathological saved configuration makes the cursor write throw and coverage degrades to prefix re-coverage rather than failing; and the SortName hint is a hint only, never the ordering authority.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/ReconciliationCursorStore.cs:26-31, 55-101, 113-140 and src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/ReconciliationCursor.cs:24-41, 111-156 (fixed kind/id, CurrentCursorVersion=1, MaxEnabledLibraryIds=4096, MaxEnabledLibraryIdLength=256, MaxSortNameHintLength=512, Validate rejects incompatible version / too many ids / blank or over-long id / empty anchor id / SortName-without-position)
src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:418-437 (AdvanceCursor contains every write failure and never fails the run)

findings.area: authentication / webhook boundary (ADR-012) and secret/lease boundary (ADR-005)
findings.summary: Re-verified unchanged at HEAD 2072ec1. The pre-binding WebhookAuthenticationFilter is still an IAsyncAuthorizationFilter on the [AllowAnonymous] controller, so MVC authenticates before model binding and no body is read for any content type; it fails closed with a uniform 401 for NotConfigured, MissingCredential and Mismatch, then rejects a declared non-JSON content type with a bounded 400 before the read; the action independently re-authenticates and applies the configured WebhookMaxPayloadBytes bound, then performs a non-blocking bounded TrySubmit. The candidate is bounded at 1024 characters before any comparison or proportional allocation, and the comparison is CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals against a version-matched lease. Secret leases fail closed on a version mismatch, render no value in ToString, add the key only as X-Api-Key and never to a URL or query, and throw after Dispose. The provider integration remains read-only: the only two HttpRequestMessage construction sites in the whole source are HttpMethod.Get. Provider errors stay bounded code-owned strings (trimmed and truncated to 512) and no secret, header, or body is reflected. The one adversarial new observation: a base URL carrying user information or a query is still accepted by validation and is still carried verbatim in ArrConnection.BaseUrl, so an operator who pastes a URL with an embedded secret would place it in the outbound URL. This is the already-carried, already-accepted SEC-14.4-04 / SEC-12 item and is INFORMATIONAL, not a new finding: the connection IDENTITY strips user information and query (verified: 'https://user:password@radarr.example:7878/?apikey=QUERY-LEAK-TRY' -> identity 'radarr:https://radarr.example:7878'), the log call sites emit only the identity, and the base URL is administrator-supplied and never attacker-controlled.

The one host-side fact the default run cannot cover (Policies.RequiresElevation evaluation for the diagnostics route) is the recorded live 401 plus the in-process MVC attribute test.

The redirect reproduction runs the shipped plugin assembly and its own DI registration directly, not inside the Jellyfin host process. The conclusion that no named provider client follows a redirect is a property of the plugin's own registration and was verified directly on the shipped binary, so no host behaviour is assumed; the only residual is whether a future host could change the plugin's named-client handlers, which the pinned-host research already says a plugin must not depend on.

The opt-in insecure-TLS relaxation is verified at the registration level (the dangerous certificate callback is retained on both .Insecure handlers while AllowAutoRedirect is false) and by executing the .Insecure clients over plain HTTP. No self-signed TLS server is stood up, so the relaxed-validation path is not exercised end to end against a real certificate. That bound predates the 21.7 fix and is unchanged by it.

The settings page's inline JavaScript cannot be executed here: the repository has no JavaScript runtime and the documented live host runs --nowebclient. The page logic was reviewed by reading it and by extracting the embedded resource from the shipped assembly and comparing it byte for byte with the source; the C# half of each feature was exercised directly (OperationalLimits range validation, PluginConfigurationValidator, the endpoint model). Any future claim about the page's runtime behaviour must keep the structural-only qualifier (already registered as V12-G6-1, V12-G8-1, V12-F3-1).

summary: Independent adversarial release security review of the CORRECTED ArrTags v1.2.0.0 release candidate (reviewed HEAD 2072ec1; artifact artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip, 619,636 bytes, SHA-256 3e59cb06dfd09da4df71e4e4a1c608b664db61326b0184c63cf846fcc502d277, MD5 f3b50a91c7cb63d9560316d8abe2f9dc, 7 entries, no SkiaSharp binary, no unexpected file, packaged ArrTags.dll byte-identical to a clean build of the audited source). reviewer_status PASS_WITH_FINDINGS with open_blocker_high = 0 and open_medium = 0, so the task 21.10 gate requirement of zero open BLOCKER/HIGH is met. SEC-21.5-01 is RESOLVED, established by my own reproduction rather than by the task reports: against the SHIPPED assembly, the corrected registration produces zero requests to the 3xx Location origin and no X-Api-Key egress, a bounded 93-character code-owned InvalidResponse/Never error with no secret, body, header, or Location content and with no response-body read at all, while a pre-fix bare-AddHttpClient control running the identical shipped client and lease code still delivers the key to the second origin - so the negative is a real fix and not a blind harness. All four named clients carry AllowAutoRedirect=false, the two opt-in insecure-TLS clients keep their relaxed certificate callback without regaining redirect-following, and the effective transport configuration is otherwise identical to the runtime's factory default (the one correction needed is informational: the .NET 10 factory default is SocketsHttpHandler, not HttpClientHandler, so the 21.7 worker's stated rationale is wrong while its conclusion is right - SEC-21.10-01). The three carried LOWs are re-verified unchanged and reproduced rather than dropped: the Cc-only control removal in the bounded log subject (SEC-21.5-02), the POSIX host treating a backslash as a file-name character and so emitting a Windows or UNC path whole (SEC-21.5-03), and the shared-temp-path state-root fallback (SEC-21.5-04); all three are optional hardening, none is a gate item, and none is a v1.2 or 21.7 regression. The remaining prior INFORMATIONAL confirmations were re-verified by reproduction against the shipped assembly: version-matched secret leases that fail closed and never render a value and never place the key in a URL, the pre-binding uniform-401 webhook filter with a 1024-character bounded candidate and a constant-time compare, the class-level elevation-gated single-GET diagnostics endpoint whose panel renders only through textContent from a fixed count-and-enum shape and fails closed, the ADR-028 page-side step check that aborts the submit before any partial POST with an independent server-side byte range, the ADR-022/ADR-029 cursor as a fixed-kind, fixed-id, versioned, integrity-checked Cache record that resets rather than trusts and whose write failure is contained, the ADR-023 re-enqueue issued after the in-flight slot is released and bounded to one per (item, connection, surface, version), the ADR-024 restore behind the single fenced write-ahead publisher, and the 20 log call sites which interpolate only a bounded subject, the secret-free connection identity, declared enums, bounded code-owned messages, and exception type names, with a throttle that never keys on the message so verbosity cannot expand a redacted value. The provider integration remains GET-only, state is written atomically with authoritative corruption quarantined and cache corruption discarded, and every path segment is validated as a single component. No new BLOCKER, HIGH, or MEDIUM was found. The only new items are two INFORMATIONAL observations (SEC-21.10-01's handler-type rationale, and SEC-21.10-02's omission of the redirect behavior change from the manifest.json one-liner), neither of which affects the release gate; the manifest point is a task 21.6 release-note completeness item for the user to decide on. The default (0/1937/66/2003), host-guarded (0/1957/46/2003), and forced-native (0/2024/21/2045) suites were all re-run by this review and equal the documented figures, with the forced-native run confirming no renderer golden regression from the transport-only change.
